about: Building knowledge as rule data (Q6210): the words the readers tell a room, a sheet, a unit, equipment and devices by. Shapes and job additions: crates/mepfix/src/wordrules.rs.

asbuilt.kind_words.source: (trade practice: the words a field markup names an element by, and its kind; moved from asbuilt.rs `NAMES`)

breakers.arc_fault_codes.source: trade practice: a panel schedule breaker code with arc-fault protection (moved from panelsched.rs)

breakers.ground_fault_codes.source: trade practice: a panel schedule breaker code with ground-fault protection (moved from panelsched.rs)

buildings.compass_names.source: drafting convention: a building named by its side of the site, written out or abbreviated (`E. BLDG`, `EAST & WEST BLDGS`), and the one name both spellings read as (Q6292)

buildings.joiners.source: drafting convention: the words and marks that join several buildings' names in one title (`EAST & WEST BLDGS`, `BUILDINGS A, B AND C`) (Q6292)

buildings.number_words.source: drafting convention: the words between a building word and its name that only say a number follows (`BUILDING NO. 2`, `BLDG #3`) (Q6292)

buildings.plural_words.source: drafting convention: the words a title names several buildings with (`EAST & WEST BLDGS`) (Q6292)

buildings.words.source: drafting convention: the words a title names one building with (`E. BLDG`, `BUILDING A`) (Q6292)

casework.callout_words.source: drafting convention: a casework or millwork detail calls a luminaire out by its type mark with one of these words (`TYPE X`, `LED STRIP LIGHT X`); the mark alone is its tag (Q6354)

casework.detail_disciplines.source: drafting convention: the disciplines whose sheets draw casework and millwork details (architectural, interiors) (Q6354)

casework.end_words.source: drafting convention: a note giving a casework luminaire's distance from the end of its casework (`6" FROM END`) has one of these (Q6354)

casework.spacing_words.source: drafting convention: a note giving casework luminaires' spacing (`2'-0" O.C.`) has one of these (Q6354)

conduit.below_slab_words.source: trade practice: a wiring method applies below the slab when its application has one of these (moved from ugplan.rs)

conduit.size_follow_words.source: drafting convention: a size followed by a word starting with one of these is a conduit's (moved from ugplan.rs)

conduit.steel_elbow_words.source: trade practice: a note with one of these calls for steel elbows (moved from ugplan.rs)

devices.ceiling_kinds.source: trade practice: the device kinds hung from or set in the ceiling (a plan's AFF note is a wall device's height, never theirs); a kind is matched in lower case with spaces as underscores (Q6244, guided.rs `ceiling_kind`)

devices.color_words.source: trade practice: a device's colour as a product record words it; the first found is the colour (moved from products.rs)

devices.designation_words.source: trade practice: designations printed beside a device symbol (GFCI, weather-resistant, tamper-resistant...); a text of only these is a subscript (moved from elec_reader.rs)

devices.device_heading_words.source: drafting convention: a schedule heading with one of these lists device types (moved from device_types.rs)

devices.kind_by_mark.source: trade practice: the kind of device a type mark names (a mark not listed: `device`) (moved from readers.rs `device_kind` and propfill.rs `kind_of`, which had the same list)

devices.known_marks.source: Marks electrical sets use with or without a legend: switches, sensors, fans, boxes, thermostats, fire-alarm and security devices. (trade practice; moved from device_types.rs `KNOWN_MARKS`)

devices.legend_kind.source: trade practice: the device a legend row's description names (value) and its IFC class (also); the first row that matches decides, a row matching when the description contains one of `any`, all of `all` and none of `none` (moved from guided.rs `legend_kind`)

devices.legend_not_device_words.source: drafting convention: a legend row whose description has one of these names no device (a mounting height note, a circuit designation, a fixture the luminaire schedule types) (moved from guided.rs `legend_kind`)

devices.legend_row_words.source: trade practice: the words a legend row describing a device of a kind (value) has; a kind not listed takes any row (moved from propfill.rs `row_fits`)

devices.mount_topics.source: The items a list names, by the words it uses: (topic, words). A device's own words (its kind, its type, its mark) name its topics the same way. (trade practice: the items a mounting-height list names (value) and its words; moved from mountlist.rs `TOPICS`)

devices.not_device_heading_words.source: drafting convention: a table heading with one of these is a panel, door, room or wall table, not a device schedule (moved from device_types.rs)

devices.not_device_table_words.source: Words of a heading whose table, a legend or a schedule all the same, lists no device types: the site, planting, material, code and structural tables (`PLANT LEGEND`, `OCCUPANT LOAD FACTOR LEGEND`, `COLUMN FOUNDATION SCHEDULE`), whose marks a device's mark can share. (drafting convention; moved from device_types.rs `NOT_DEVICE_TYPES`)

devices.receptacle_designations.source: (trade practice: a receptacle's designations (value) and the words printed for them; moved from guided.rs `DESIGNATIONS`)

devices.typical_height_kind.source: trade practice: the kind a typical-height note's item names; the first row whose word the item contains decides (moved from guided.rs `typical_kind`)

equipment.air_device_system.source: trade practice: an air device mark's letters and the air system it serves (CD-1: supply) (moved from equip_reader.rs)

equipment.control_marks.source: drafting practice: the marks of the controls and sensors a unit's tag labels when printed beside them (a thermostat, a humidistat, a sensor, a switch: `FCU-1 T` is the thermostat of FCU-1, not the unit) (fix-symbol-misread)

equipment.floor_mounting_words.source: trade practice: a mounting with one of these stands on the floor (moved from concrete.rs `needs_pad`)

equipment.gear_submittal_words.source: The gear words a submittal's file name carries when it is a gear submittal. (trade practice; moved from guided.rs `GEAR_SUBMITTAL_WORDS`)

equipment.in_wall_mounting_words.source: drafting convention: the words a schedule's MOUNTING says a panel is set into its wall by (`RECESSED`, `FLUSH`); anything else hangs on the wall's face (Q6513)

equipment.gear_location_phrases.source: drafting convention: the words a riser or one-line label, or a plan note, puts between a panel's name and the room it is in (`PANEL 'A' LOCATED IN ELEC 1120`, a label's next line `MOUNTED IN STORAGE 1104`); the longest first (Q6513)

schedules.panel_location_labels.source: drafting convention: the header labels a panel schedule names the panel's room by (`LOCATION:`, `MOUNTED IN:`), in the order they are trusted (Q6513)

equipment.switchboard_words.source: drafting convention: the words that name a switchboard or switchgear on a plan's label or a schedule's header (`SWBD MDP`); the word and the tag after it label the gear (Q6437)

equipment.kind_by_tag_prefix.source: trade practice: an equipment tag's letters and the kind they name (AHU-1: ahu) (moved from equip_reader.rs `kind_from_tag`)

equipment.kind_by_title_words.source: trade practice: an equipment schedule's title words and the kind of what its rows are, the first pair whose words the title has (a heat pump is no pump, a fan coil unit no fan, a packaged terminal unit no rooftop unit); read before equip_reader.rs `kind_from_title`'s own words (Q6313)

equipment.load_words.source: trade practice: a panel schedule load whose description has one of these is a piece of equipment (its connection is the device) (moved from guided.rs `equipment_load`)

equipment.marks.source: Equipment marks, which are not air devices' tags. (trade practice; moved from duct_reader.rs `EQUIPMENT_MARKS`)

equipment.maybe_pad_kinds.source: Equipment set on the floor or grade only when its mounting or elevation says so. (trade practice: equipment that stands on a pad when it is on the floor; moved from concrete.rs `MAYBE_KINDS`)

equipment.names.source: Words of equipment and device tags, never a room's name (`PNLBD 'D'`, `XFMR T1`, `DISC`). (trade practice: words of an equipment label; moved from geometry.rs `EQUIPMENT_WORDS`)

equipment.off_floor_mounting_words.source: trade practice: a mounting with one of these is off the floor: no pad (moved from concrete.rs `needs_pad`)

equipment.pad_kinds.source: Equipment always set on the floor or grade (unless its mounting says otherwise). (trade practice: equipment that stands on a housekeeping pad; moved from concrete.rs `FLOOR_KINDS`)

equipment.room_unit_tags.source: trade practice: the printed tags of a room's own equipment (a tag alone or with -n) and its kind: EF an exhaust fan, PTAC a packaged terminal unit; a typical panel's load and a device so tagged are its connection (moved from guided.rs)

equipment.submittal_package_words.source: The submittals at `paths`: each PDF (or a submittal's text, `.txt`) given, and those in each folder given (not its subfolders), in name order. Words of a submittal package's name that say it holds products the model's elements are. (trade practice: the words a product submittal's package name carries; moved from submittals.rs `PRODUCT_PACKAGE_WORDS`)

equipment.tag_kind.source: trade practice: the kind of equipment a tag beside a duct-plan box names; the first row whose word the tag has decides (`word:EF` a whole word, else a part of the tag) (moved from duct_reader.rs)

equipment.tag_prefix_kind.source: trade practice: the kind of equipment a schedule tag starting so names (FCU-1: fan coil unit); the first row whose word the tag starts with decides (moved from duct_reader.rs)

equipment.tags.source: Marks that tag mechanical equipment (`HP` over its number: heat pump 3). A device so marked is that equipment's electrical connection. (trade practice; moved from guided.rs `EQUIPMENT_TAGS`)

equipment.typical_load_words.source: trade practice: the words a typical panel's load names a room's equipment by, per equipment kind (value) (moved from guided.rs)

finishes.floor_patterns.source: trade practice: the patterned layouts a floor code names (moved from finishes.rs `pattern_of`)

finishes.paint_sheens.source: trade practice: the paint sheens a finish legend names; the first the description contains is taken (SEMIGLOSS reads as SEMI-GLOSS) (moved from finishes.rs `parse_sheen`)

fixtures.emergency_words.source: trade practice: a fixture type whose description or lamp has one of these is emergency or exit lighting; the first found is the reason given (moved from lighting.rs)

fixtures.exterior_words.source: trade practice: a luminaire whose description has one of these is not interior lighting (moved from lighting.rs)

fixtures.finish_words.source: (trade practice: a luminaire finish as printed, and its name; moved from lighting.rs `FINISHES`)

fixtures.kind_by_description.source: (trade practice: a schedule description's words and the fixture kind; the first word a description contains decides; moved from casework_reader.rs `WORDS`)

fixtures.lighting_words.source: Each product's dimming (`dimming_of`) from its catalog number and its pages, and whether it is a luminaire (its pages speak of lumens, LEDs, CCT…). A product whose pages name several controls with nothing saying which was ordered is a question. Words a lighting cut sheet uses of its product; a product whose pages use two of them is a luminaire. (trade practice; moved from spec_import.rs `LIGHTING_WORDS`)

fixtures.luminaire_words.source: trade practice: a schedule row whose description has one of these is a luminaire (moved from guided.rs `schedule_row_kind`)

fixtures.wall_mount_words.source: A luminaire whose cut sheet says it goes on a wall (not the wall-wash trims of a downlight). (trade practice; moved from spec_import.rs `WALL_MOUNT_WORDS`)

fp.head_kinds.source: Words of a sprinkler head legend or schedule row and the head kind they name, first match wins (NFPA 13 head orientations: sidewall, upright, pendent; concealed and recessed heads hang pendent; Q6497).

fp.head_table_titles.source: Titles of the head table a sprinkler shop drawing counts its heads in (drafting convention; Q6497).

fp.page_words.source: Words a page's own text names fire protection by: a page that prints none is no sprinkler plan (trade vocabulary; Q6497).

fp.quantity_headers.source: Column headings of a table's count column (drafting convention; Q6497).

fp.shop_drawing_path_words.source: Words in a submittal file's or folder's name that make it a fire protection submittal whose pages are read for sprinkler shop drawings (trade vocabulary and the CSI MasterFormat 21 13 13 wet-pipe sprinkler section number; Q6497).

fp.submittal_folder_words.source: Words in the name of a folder beside the prints that make it the project's submittals (looked in for sprinkler shop drawings when the job is given none; Q6497).

framing.layout_heading_words.source: (drafting convention: the words of a joist or floor framing layout's heading that names the floor it is for, `2ND FLOOR FRAMING`, `LEVEL 3 JOIST LAYOUT`; Q6400)

framing.typical_note_words.source: (drafting convention: the words that make a framing plan's note the floor's typical framing, `TYP.`, `U.N.O.` (unless noted otherwise); one with a full stop is matched as written, the others as whole words; Q6400)

keynotes.box_words.source: trade practice: a keynote with one of these names a box (its size is read) (moved from keynotes.rs)

keynotes.buried_words.source: The words a note uses for work in the ground or under the slab. (trade practice; moved from keynotes.rs `BURIED_WORDS`)

keynotes.hard_lid_words.source: The words that put a run over a hard (gypsum board) ceiling. (trade practice; moved from keynotes.rs `HARD_LID_WORDS`)

keynotes.pull_words.source: The words a note gives a conduit's pull line with. (trade practice; moved from keynotes.rs `PULL_WORDS`)

keys.building_words.source: trade practice: a key count stated about these is the building's (moved from guided.rs `stated_keys`)

keys.not_building_words.source: trade practice: a key count stated with one of these is a lock's, a panel's or a door's, not the building's (moved from guided.rs `stated_keys`)

layers.stair_words.source: drafting convention: layer-name parts of a stair or ramp layer (moved from stairs.rs)

levels.finish_floor_mark_words.source: drafting convention: a level marker on a section or elevation that names the finished floor without a level number (`FIN. FLR. EL. 100'-0"`); in a building of one storey it is that storey's floor. Compared word for word, punctuation and EL/ELEV ignored (Q6286)

levels.first_floor_words.source: trade practice: a level named with one of these is the first floor (moved from sheet_reader.rs `is_first_floor_word`)

levels.mezzanine_words.source: drafting convention: a plan title with one of these words is the plan of a mezzanine (`MEZZANINE PLAN`, `MEZZ. LIGHTING PLAN`), a partial floor inside the storey under it; its level code is `M`, ranked between its floor and the next (Q6322, sheet_reader.rs `detect_levels`)

levels.open_below_words.source: drafting convention: a label on a mezzanine's (or any upper floor's) plan marking a space with no floor, open to the storey under it (`OPEN TO BELOW`); the space is left out of the level's floor slab (Q6322, wallgen.rs). Compared word for word, punctuation ignored

levels.plate_mark_words.source: drafting convention: a level marker on a section or elevation at the top of the wall plate or the masonry bearing wall, where the roof framing bears (`T.O. PLATE 112'-0"`, `TOP OF CMU 10'-0"`); when no roof level is marked it gives the roof's elevation. A truss or joist bearing mark (`TRUSS BEARING 121'-4"`, `TRUSS BRG. ELEV.`) is the same line: where the roof framing sits (Q6314). Compared word for word, punctuation and EL/ELEV ignored (Q6286)

notes.appliance_words.source: trade practice: an appliance a mounting-height note names (`MICROWAVE 65" AFF` on a leader): the note gives the height of the receptacle or connection that feeds it, never a switch's (Q6244, guided.rs `typical_heights`)

notes.defer_to_architecture.source: drafting convention: an electrical sheet's numbered note that sends its devices' locations or mounting heights to the architecture's drawings (`SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DEVICE LOCATIONS AND HEIGHTS`, `MOUNT AT THE HEIGHT SHOWN ON THE ARCHITECTURAL ELEVATIONS`): value is what it sends there (both, heights, locations); the first row that matches decides, a row matching when the note contains one of `any` and all of `all` (Q6244, archauthority.rs)

notes.reference_only.source: drafting convention: a sheet's note that says its layout or its device spots are for reference only or diagrammatic (`LOW VOLTAGE LAYOUT IS FOR REFERENCE ONLY`, `DEVICE LOCATIONS ARE DIAGRAMMATIC`): its spots are not measured against (Q6262, validate_present.rs); a row matches when the note contains one of `any`, all of `all` and none of `none` (a background drawn for reference, raceways drawn diagrammatically are no such note)

openings.window_mark_prefixes.source: drafting convention: a window's tag on a floor plan is its type letter and a number (`W5`, `W-2`, `W3A`); a mark so by a gap in an outside wall is a window there when the set has no window schedule to read the marks from (Q6293, wallgen.rs `is_window_mark`)

openings.storefront_mark_prefixes.source: drafting convention: a storefront's tag on a floor plan is its type letters and a number (`SF1`, `SF-2`); it is a window mark whose window is a storefront assembly (Q6311, wallgen.rs `storefront_mark`)

openings.storefront_words.source: door and window schedules and legends: a type or frame of these words is a storefront or curtain-wall assembly, from the floor up when the schedule gives no sill (Q6311, wallgen.rs `storefront_mark`)

pipes.drain_systems.source: The drainage services (sanitary, waste, storm) a stack base or a slab drain belongs to. (trade practice; moved from ugplan.rs `DRAINS`)

pipes.plan_title_system_words.source: drafting convention: a plan title with one of these names a piping system (moved from printmep.rs)

pipes.sanitary_title_words.source: drafting convention: a plan title with one of these words draws the sanitary system (moved from mep.rs)

pipes.system_letters.source: Printed pipe system letters → our codes. (trade practice; moved from equip_reader.rs `PIPE_ABBR`)

pipes.water_systems.source: (trade practice: the water systems a floor's plumbing plan draws; moved from guided.rs `WATER`)

roof.curb_words.source: Curbs and openings on a roof that aren't units: their notes give a curb or a height. (trade practice; moved from exterior.rs `CURB_WORDS`)

roof.drain_words.source: Notes a roof plan writes on its roof (the seeds for finding it; not its title's `ROOF`). (trade practice; moved from exterior.rs `ROOF_WORDS`)

roof.equipment_words.source: Words naming what stands on a roof. (trade practice; moved from exterior.rs `EQUIPMENT_WORDS`)

rooms.area_units.source: A room's printed area is a figure and one of these units, spaces and dots left out (105 SF, 1,960 S.F., 12 SQ FT): never the room's name. (drafting convention)

rooms.corridor_words.source: trade practice: a route named with one of these runs along any corridor of the level (moved from guided.rs)

rooms.equipment_label_words.source: trade practice: electrical gear abbreviations; a room label with one looks like equipment, not a room name (asked) (moved from guided.rs `run_rooms`)

rooms.equipment_room_names.source: trade practice: an equipment room's names (the trades' plans call it MEP, the architect MECH); a view title naming one names the same room (moved from guided.rs `room_of_view`)

rooms.finish_codes.source: Run the rooms stage: detect rooms from labels (MUST 1, 4). Uses the same readers (rooms.list) that work directly on the job's sheets. Finish and material codes of the finish legend (gypsum board, carpet, vinyl and ceramic tile, acoustic tile, paint, rubber base, wood, epoxy, sealed concrete): a tag of one is no room. (drafting convention: finish legend codes; moved from guided.rs `FINISH_CODES`)

rooms.habitable.source: Words of a room to sleep or live in (a unit type, a bedroom), for [`HABITABLE_MIN_SF`]. (trade practice; moved from geometry.rs `HABITABLE_WORDS`)

rooms.names.source: Words of a room's tag: unit types and the rooms a plan names. (trade practice: words of a room's name; moved from geometry.rs `ROOM_WORDS`)

rooms.not_room_words.source: Words that put a label in a title block, a stamp or the notes, never on a room: the firm and its address, the review and issue stamps, the sheet's and views' titles. (drafting convention; moved from autospec.rs `NOT_ROOM_WORDS`)

rooms.not_rooms.source: (drafting convention: names that are clearly not rooms (building materials, notes, structural and finish labels); moved from guided.rs `NOT_ROOMS`)

rooms.sleeping.source: (trade practice: the type words of a room to sleep in, a hotel's guest room (QUEEN, KING, SUITE) or a dwelling unit; moved from guided.rs `SLEEPING`)

rooms.space_kind_words.source: trade practice: the first word of a space's name that makes it a corridor, a stair or a hoistway (value: corridor, stair, hoistway) (moved from wallgen.rs)

rooms.specialty_rooms.source: trade practice: the room names whose specialties (bath accessories, wardrobe rod, toilet accessories, corner guards, extinguisher cabinet) the company standard places until the documents show them, per room use (value); the rule text and items stay in finishes.rs (moved from finishes.rs `room_rules`)

schedules.equipment_table_words.source: drafting convention: a table whose heading has one of these schedules equipment (an electrical connection each) (moved from guided.rs `schedule_row_kind`)

schedules.luminaire_table_words.source: drafting convention: a table whose heading has one of these schedules luminaires (moved from guided.rs `schedule_row_kind`)

schedules.luminaire_titles.source: drafting convention: the titles of a luminaire schedule (moved from guided.rs); read on any trade's sheet (fix-lum-fixture-schedule-not-read)

schedules.electrical_luminaire_titles.source: drafting convention: on an electrical sheet a plain FIXTURE SCHEDULE is the luminaire schedule (fix-lum-fixture-schedule-not-read)

schedules.not_luminaire_title_words.source: drafting convention: a schedule title naming another trade's or another table's fixtures is no luminaire schedule, nor is the table of a schedule's notes (LIGHTING FIXTURE SCHEDULE NOTES) (fix-lum-fixture-schedule-not-read, fix-fixture-schedule-type-column-unread)

schedules.title_reference_words.source: grammar of drawing notes: words that make a line naming a schedule a note sending the reader to it (`... ON LIGHT FIXTURE SCHEDULE.`, `SEE ... FIXTURE SCHEDULE`), not the schedule's title (fix-lum-fixture-schedule-not-read)

schedules.luminaire_type_headings.source: format vocabulary of luminaire schedules: the headings of the column of type marks, tried in this order; a column headed FIXTURE alone holds the marks too (fix-lum-fixture-schedule-not-read)

schedules.not_mark_heading_words.source: format vocabulary of luminaire schedules: words of a column heading that name another field than the fixture's mark, so a TYPE under them is not the mark column (a lamp's TYPE under the LAMPS group heading, a MOUNTING TYPE, a VOLTAGE) (fix-lum-schedule-type-column-wrong)

schedules.voltage_words.source: electrical trade vocabulary: the voltage designations a luminaire schedule prints in its voltage column (multi-volt and universal drivers), never a type mark (fix-lum-schedule-type-column-wrong)

schedules.voltage_units.source: electrical trade vocabulary: the units a voltage is printed with (277V, 24VDC, 120VAC), so a number with one of them is a voltage, never a type mark (fix-lum-schedule-type-column-wrong)

schedules.variant_lead_words.source: grammar of schedule notes: the words that lead a list of fixture marks (`FIXTURES AE, BE AND CE ARE ...`) (fix-lum-fixture-schedule-not-read)

schedules.plumbing_fixture_titles.source: drafting convention: the titles of a plumbing fixture schedule; read on any trade's sheet, not only the plumbing sheets (fix-plumbing-fixtures-zero)

schedules.mark_headings.source: format vocabulary of construction schedules: the headings of a schedule's column of marks; the marks under one are that schedule's items (fix-symbol-misread)

schedules.opening_mark_words.source: format vocabulary of door and window schedules: the last word of the heading of the column of marks (`MARK`, `DOOR NO.`, `WINDOW #`) (fix-title-block-read-as-schedule-rows)

schedules.opening_mark_qualifiers.source: format vocabulary of door and window schedules: the words that may come before the mark word in the heading of the column of marks (`DOOR NO.`, `OPENING MARK`); a heading with any other word is a title-block field (`PROJECT NO.`, `SHEET NO.`), not a column of marks (fix-title-block-read-as-schedule-rows)

schedules.not_marks.source: drafting convention: short title-block and stamp field labels that look like a code but are never a door or window mark (`NO.`, `BY`, `REV`, `DWG`) (fix-title-block-read-as-schedule-rows)

sheets.device_disciplines.source: The disciplines whose sheets draw devices (electrical, mechanical, plumbing, fire protection and alarm, technology). (drafting convention; moved from guided.rs `DEVICE_DISCIPLINES`)

sheets.discipline_letters.source: Sheet-number letters that name a discipline. A sheet found only by its largest sheet-number lettering counts when it is one of these: equipment marks look like sheet numbers too (`RTU-1`, `EF-2`). (drafting convention; moved from readers.rs `DISCIPLINES`)

sheets.discipline_prefix.source: Known discipline prefixes: sheet number prefix → discipline code. (drafting convention: the sheet-number letters of a discipline; moved from sheet_reader.rs `DISCIPLINE_PREFIX`)

sheets.number_prefixes.source: drafting convention (the national CAD standard's sheet identification): the letters a sheet number may start with, a discipline designator alone or with the modifier sets use; any other letters (an equipment or schedule tag read in the drawing area) make a sheet number suspect

sheets.discipline_words.source: drafting convention: a word that names a discipline, and its letter (moved from printlinks.rs `discipline_word`)

sheets.specification_title_words.source: A sheet title that says the sheet is a specification printed on the drawings (`ELECTRICAL SPECIFICATIONS`), not a plan. (drafting convention: general, no job's title)

sheets.floor_plan_title_words.source: A view or sheet title that names a floor plan. (drafting convention: general, no job's title)

sheets.import_discipline_prefix.source: Known discipline prefixes: sheet number prefix → discipline code. (drafting convention: the sheet-number letters of a discipline, as the import check reads them; moved from import_check.rs `DISCIPLINE_PREFIX`)

sheets.mechanical_title_words.source: drafting convention: a view title with one of these is a mechanical view (moved from guided.rs)

sheets.mount_note_disciplines.source: The disciplines whose sheets that aren't plans may list mounting heights in their notes: the general (accessibility) sheets, the architecture's, the trades'. (drafting convention; moved from guided.rs `MOUNT_NOTE_DISCIPLINES`)

schedules.panel_title_not_tags.source: (panel schedule convention: words that follow PANEL in a heading, a label or a header field but are not the panel's tag: PANEL SCHEDULE, PANEL NAME:, PANELBOARD NOTES, PANEL SIZE & TYPE:, PANEL LOCATION:)

schedules.panel_circuit_headings.source: (panel schedule convention: the heading over the circuit-number column, as sets print it: CKT, CIR, CIRC, CIRCUIT, CKT #, CKT NO.)

schedules.panel_header_words.source: (panel schedule column headings as printed: breaker amps, poles, breaker type, load categories, circuit number, phases; a header line of only these words is several columns' names read as one text)

sheets.subdiscipline_codes.source: (US National CAD Standard sheet designators: a discipline letter and a modifier letter name a sub-discipline of that trade, e.g. EP electrical power, EL electrical lighting, AS architectural site/shell, MH mechanical HVAC, PL plumbing; such a sheet is its trade's)

sheets.site_part_words.source: (drafting convention: a view title that starts with one of these words and an identifier — a number, or one letter — names the part of the site the view draws, as BUILDING 2 - UNIT 6; each word with the kind of part it names)

sheets.non_building_disciplines.source: (drafting convention: the disciplines that don't carry building walls and doors (life safety, fire protection, fire alarm, general/civil, structural, telecom); moved from guided.rs `NON_BUILDING`)

sheets.not_plan_view_words.source: View-title words that never name a plan. (drafting convention; moved from printlinks.rs `NOT_PLAN_WORDS`)

sheets.plan_view_words.source: A view-title word that names a plan of some kind (floor, roof, ceiling, enlarged), for the scale a sheet's plans print at; a title with one of sheets.not_plan_view_words is no plan. (drafting convention: general, no job's title)

sheets.other_plan_title_words.source: A view title that names a plan which is not the floor plan, though it can share the floor plan's sheet and draw the same outline: the ceiling, the roof, the structure or the demolition. (drafting convention: general, no job's title)

sheets.reference_words.source: Words of a title that make a sheet or view a reference one (not a plan to read runs off). (drafting convention; moved from printmep.rs `REFERENCE_WORDS`)

sheets.site_disciplines.source: drafting convention: the sheet-number disciplines of civil, landscape and site sheets (moved from sheet_facts.rs)

sheets.site_title_words.source: (drafting convention: the words of a site or civil sheet's title; moved from sheet_facts.rs `SITE_WORDS`)

sheets.title_discipline.source: drafting convention: the words of a sheet title or keynote header that name its discipline (value); the first group whose word the title contains decides (moved from guided.rs `infer_discipline_from_title`)

sheets.trade_heading_words.source: drafting convention: the words a table heading names a trade by, per discipline letter (value) (moved from guided.rs `trade_names`)

sheets.underground_trade_prefix.source: drafting convention: a callout's sheet-number letters and the trade whose underground work it is (E, P) (moved from ugplan.rs)

sheets.valid_prefixes.source: drafting convention: the discipline letters a sheet number starts with (moved from printset.rs)

sheets.view_title_words.source: (drafting convention: the words of a view title that are the view's own (ENLARGED, PLAN, the trade, the floor), not a room's name; moved from guided.rs `VIEW_WORDS`)

site.asphalt_words.source: trade practice: a paving label with one of these is asphalt (moved from sitetakeoff.rs)

site.concrete_words.source: trade practice: a paving label with one of these is concrete (moved from sitetakeoff.rs)

site.contour_layer_words.source: (drafting convention: civil layer-name parts; moved from sitetakeoff.rs `CONTOUR_LAYER`)

site.existing_words.source: (drafting convention: civil layer-name parts; moved from sitetakeoff.rs `EXISTING_WORDS`)

site.fence_layer_words.source: (drafting convention: civil layer-name parts; moved from sitetakeoff.rs `FENCE_LAYER`)

site.frame_layer_words.source: The sheet's frame and title block: never site work. (drafting convention: layer-name parts of a sheet's frame and title block; moved from sitetakeoff.rs `FRAME_LAYER`)

site.paving_words.source: trade practice: a site text with one of these labels paving (moved from sitetakeoff.rs)

site.structure_layer_words.source: (drafting convention: civil layer-name parts; moved from sitetakeoff.rs `STRUCTURE_LAYER`)

site.utility_layer_words.source: (drafting convention: civil layer-name parts; moved from sitetakeoff.rs `UTILITY_LAYER`)

site.utility_system_words.source: trade practice: a civil text's word and the utility system it names (moved from sitetakeoff.rs `system_of`)

specs.location_words.source: trade practice: location words of a specification or general note's location rule (moved from spec_import.rs `extract_location_rule`)

specs.sheet_pointer_words.source: The words a project manual points a division to a drawing sheet by (`Refer Sheet E4.1 for Electrical Specifications`, `See Sheets ME-4.1 and ME-4.2`, `specifications are on Drawing P4.1`), with a word of specs.sheet_words before the sheet numbers. (CSI project manual practice: a small job's MEP specifications printed on the drawings)

specs.sheet_words.source: The words before a drawing sheet's number in a project manual's pointer to it (specs.sheet_pointer_words). (drafting convention)

specs.product_divisions.source: The CSI divisions whose sections speak for the model's devices, fixtures and equipment. (MasterFormat divisions; moved from products.rs `PRODUCT_DIVISIONS`)

specs.raceway_words.source: trade practice: wiring-method words of a specification or general note's location rule (moved from spec_import.rs `extract_location_rule`)

tags.not_panel_words.source: Words lettered before a dash that are no panel's name (`NOTE-1`, `TYPE-2`). (drafting convention; moved from printcond.rs `NOT_PANELS`)

tags.not_type_tags.source: Words a submittal's form prints where a type tag goes that are no type. (drafting convention: a submittal form's words; moved from guided.rs `NOT_TYPE_TAGS`)

tags.conductor_note_words.source: drafting convention: the words a conductor note prints after a size (`3#10 THHN`, `1#10G`, `1#10 EG`, `1/0 AL`): a role, an insulation, a metal, a unit. Any other word after a size, or before the `#` where a count goes (`PUMP #2`), makes the text a label, not a conductor note

tags.note_words.source: Words that are short and capitalised but are notes, not type tags. (drafting convention: plan-note abbreviations; moved from sheet_facts.rs `NOT_TAGS`)

tags.panel_prefix_words.source: drafting convention: the words a panel's lettering starts with (`PANEL LA`); the first that the lettering starts with is taken off (moved from printcond.rs)

units.dropped_type_words.source: trade practice: words a room type's name carries that don't tell its types apart (moved from guided.rs `type_words`)

units.not_unit_words.source: trade practice: equipment named like a unit (UNIT HEATER, UNIT VENTILATOR) and notes: a tag with one of these names no unit type (moved from unittypes.rs)

units.packaged_unit_words.source: trade practice: a unit legend item with one of these words is a packaged terminal unit (kind ptac) (moved from unit_reader.rs `kind_of`)

units.type_word_aliases.source: trade practice: a room type's word and the word it is written as (QUEEN as Q, ACCESSIBLE as ADA) (moved from guided.rs `type_words`)

units.type_words.source: Words that start a unit type's tag (`ADA KING`, `UNIT B`, `TYPE A1`). (trade practice: the words of a typical unit's type; moved from unittypes.rs `UNIT_WORDS`)

units.typical_view_words.source: drafting convention: a view title that has one of these is a unit's, a typical one or a room's (moved from guided.rs `room_view`)

units.unit_plan_title_words.source: trade practice: an enlarged plan whose title has one of these draws a typical unit (moved from guided.rs)

walls.room_side_words.source: trade practice: the room names either side of an untagged wall that pick its type, per wall use (value: corridor, wet, acoustic) (moved from wall_reader.rs)

walls.type_name_words.source: trade practice: the words of the wall type's name each wall use (value) takes: the corridor type, the plumbing wall, the acoustic one (moved from wall_reader.rs)
